level: serious amateur aiming at professional competence

schools.name: Spec-first school
schools.optimises_for: predictable scope — writing a short spec before generating code so the AI's first pass matches what was actually asked
schools.gives_up: the momentum of just typing a prompt and seeing what comes back

schools.name: Vibe-loop school
schools.optimises_for: fast conversational iteration — prompt, run, look, refine — treating the running app as the source of truth over any written spec
schools.gives_up: predictable architecture; the codebase's shape emerges from the conversation instead of being decided upfront

schools.name: Verification-first school
schools.optimises_for: catching AI mistakes before they merge — diffs read line by line, tests demanded for every change, types and checks as hard gates
schools.gives_up: raw throughput; every AI change costs a review pass before it counts as done

schools.name: Agentic-autonomy school
schools.optimises_for: letting a coding agent run multi-step tasks unattended — plan, edit, run, fix — with the human reviewing outcomes, not keystrokes
schools.gives_up: fine-grained control over exactly how a change gets made, and the ability to catch a wrong turn mid-task

schools.name: Manual-gate school
schools.optimises_for: a human decision at every consequential step — every diff read, every command approved, before it touches the real codebase
schools.gives_up: throughput and the ability to hand off long-running or overnight tasks to an agent

clusters.name: Prompt & spec craft
clusters.gist: Turning an intent into a prompt an AI can actually execute: framing context, decomposing tasks, writing specs, and recovering when the first answer is wrong.

clusters.name: Frontend generation
clusters.gist: Building the interface with AI assistance, from one static page to a component-driven, accessible frontend wired to a real API.

clusters.name: Verifying AI output
clusters.gist: Treating generated code the way you'd treat a junior engineer's PR: reading diffs, spotting hallucinated APIs, and gating merges on tests and types.

clusters.name: Iterative workflow
clusters.gist: Running the prompt-run-refine loop without losing control: session scoping, checkpoint commits, and knowing when to roll back instead of prompting harder.

clusters.name: Backend & data
clusters.gist: Endpoints, schemas, auth, and validation built with AI assistance but understood well enough to defend every line.

clusters.name: Agentic tooling
clusters.gist: Moving from single-file inline suggestions to agents that edit multiple files, run commands, and complete bounded tasks unattended.

clusters.name: Deployment & ops
clusters.gist: Shipping an AI-assisted app to production: environment config, CI gates, rollback paths, and the monitoring that turns failures into alerts instead of complaints.

clusters.name: System architecture & scale
clusters.gist: Keeping a growing AI-assisted codebase coherent: conventions, boundaries, tech-debt triage, and the judgment call between another patch and a real restructure.

nodes.label: Context framing
nodes.one_line: Frame a prompt with the goal, relevant files, and constraints so a coding assistant's first response is usable without a rewrite.

nodes.label: Task decomposition
nodes.one_line: Break a feature request into AI-sized subtasks small enough that each one's output can be checked on its own.

nodes.label: Spec writing
nodes.one_line: Write a short spec — inputs, outputs, edge cases — before generating code so scope is fixed before the assistant starts.

nodes.label: Example anchoring
nodes.one_line: Anchor a prompt to an existing file or example so generated code matches the project's actual patterns instead of generic ones.

nodes.label: Constraint declaration
nodes.one_line: State explicit boundaries — files not to touch, libraries not to add — so an AI edit can't quietly expand past its task.

nodes.label: Diagnostic reprompting
nodes.one_line: Diagnose exactly where a wrong AI output missed the ask, then rewrite the prompt to close that specific gap instead of repeating it verbatim.

nodes.label: Prompt templates
nodes.one_line: Save and reuse prompt templates for recurring task shapes (new component, new endpoint, bug fix) so context-gathering isn't rebuilt from scratch every time.

nodes.label: Single-page scaffold
nodes.one_line: Generate a static HTML/CSS/JS page from a prompt and get it rendering correctly in a browser on the first or second pass.

nodes.label: Component extraction
nodes.one_line: Ask an assistant to split a monolithic page into reusable components without changing what the page does.

nodes.label: Framework adoption
nodes.one_line: Move a static page into a framework (React, Vue, Svelte) with AI generating correct component boilerplate, checked spec-first and diff-by-diff.

nodes.label: Styling system
nodes.one_line: Direct AI-generated styling toward a consistent system — tokens, a utility framework — instead of one-off inline styles per component.

nodes.label: State management
nodes.one_line: Get an assistant to wire up state — local state, forms, a simple store — correctly across components instead of duplicating it per screen.

nodes.label: API integration (client)
nodes.one_line: Wire a frontend to a real API client with AI assistance, handling loading and error states, not just the happy path.

nodes.label: Responsive & accessible layout
nodes.one_line: Direct AI output toward responsive layout and basic accessibility — labels, contrast, keyboard nav — instead of visual-only correctness.

nodes.label: Component library
nodes.one_line: Build or adopt a shared component library so AI-generated screens draw from one consistent set instead of reinventing components each time.

nodes.label: Diff reading
nodes.one_line: Read an AI-generated diff line by line before accepting it, not just skim the changed file list.

nodes.label: Hallucination spotting
nodes.one_line: Recognize a hallucinated API, package, or function signature by checking it against real docs before running it.

nodes.label: Manual smoke test
nodes.one_line: Run the actual feature by hand after an AI change instead of trusting that it compiled.

nodes.label: Unit test generation
nodes.one_line: Have an assistant write tests for the behavior it just implemented, then check the tests actually assert the right thing.

nodes.label: Type-checking gate
nodes.one_line: Run the type checker after every AI edit and treat a type error as a required gate, not a suggestion to ignore.

nodes.label: Regression check
nodes.one_line: Run the existing test suite after an AI change to catch regressions the AI's own tests wouldn't reveal.

nodes.label: Review checklist
nodes.one_line: Apply a fixed checklist — security, error handling, edge cases — to AI-generated code the way you'd review a junior engineer's pull request.

nodes.label: Session scoping
nodes.one_line: Keep one AI session focused on a single task so context doesn't drift across unrelated changes.

nodes.label: Git checkpointing
nodes.one_line: Commit after each verified AI change so a bad iteration is one git reset away, not a lost afternoon.

nodes.label: Context-window management
nodes.one_line: Recognize when a session's context is degrading — contradicting itself, forgetting earlier constraints — and start fresh instead of pushing through.

nodes.label: Diff-sized commits
nodes.one_line: Keep each AI-assisted commit small enough to review and revert independently.

nodes.label: Branch per feature
nodes.one_line: Run each AI-assisted feature on its own branch so a failed experiment doesn't contaminate main.

nodes.label: Rollback discipline
nodes.one_line: Recognize when an AI session has gone sideways and roll back to the last good checkpoint instead of prompting your way out.

nodes.label: Session handoff notes
nodes.one_line: Write a short state note at the end of a session so the next session — yours or the AI's — resumes without re-deriving context.

nodes.label: REST endpoint scaffold
nodes.one_line: Generate a REST endpoint — route, handler, response — with AI assistance and get it responding correctly to a real request.

nodes.label: Schema design
nodes.one_line: Design a database schema, by hand or with AI assistance, well enough to defend every table and relationship in it.

nodes.label: ORM wiring
nodes.one_line: Have an assistant wire an ORM or query layer to the schema and verify the generated queries actually match the intended relationships.

nodes.label: Auth flow
nodes.one_line: Implement a real authentication flow — sessions or tokens — with AI assistance, understanding every step well enough to spot a missing check.

nodes.label: Input validation
nodes.one_line: Add server-side validation and sanitization to AI-generated endpoints so the client is never trusted with the last word.

nodes.label: Migration discipline
nodes.one_line: Generate and review database migrations with AI, checking that each one is reversible and doesn't silently drop data.

nodes.label: Error-handling contract
nodes.one_line: Define and enforce a consistent error-response contract across AI-generated endpoints instead of an ad hoc shape per route.

nodes.label: Background jobs
nodes.one_line: Move slow or scheduled work into background jobs or queues with AI assistance, verifying failure and retry behavior by hand.

nodes.label: Inline assistant use
nodes.one_line: Use an inline AI coding assistant — completion, inline edit — inside the editor for single-file changes.

nodes.label: Chat-to-code loop
nodes.one_line: Run the basic chat loop: describe a change, receive a diff or file, apply it, check the result.

nodes.label: Multi-file agent tasks
nodes.one_line: Direct an agentic coding tool to make a coordinated change across multiple files in a single task.

nodes.label: Tool permission scoping
nodes.one_line: Configure what an agent may do unattended — read-only, edit, run commands — and set that scope deliberately per task.

nodes.label: Command execution review
nodes.one_line: Review a shell command an agent proposes before letting it run, especially anything destructive or network-facing.

nodes.label: Custom agent instructions
nodes.one_line: Write persistent project instructions — a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md-style file — that steer every future agent session's defaults.

nodes.label: Autonomous task delegation
nodes.one_line: Hand a bounded multi-step task to an agent to run unattended, with a clear definition of done and a way to check the result.

nodes.label: Multi-agent coordination
nodes.one_line: Run multiple agents on independent parts of a codebase in parallel without their changes stepping on each other.

nodes.label: Static hosting
nodes.one_line: Deploy a static site to a host from a repo and get a working public URL.

nodes.label: Environment config
nodes.one_line: Separate configuration and secrets from code using environment variables, correctly scoped per environment.

nodes.label: CI pipeline
nodes.one_line: Set up a CI pipeline that runs tests and checks on every AI-assisted commit before it can merge.

nodes.label: Full-stack deploy
nodes.one_line: Deploy a full-stack app — frontend, backend, database — with every piece correctly wired to the others in production.

nodes.label: Rollback plan
nodes.one_line: Set up a deployment rollback path so a bad AI-assisted release can be reverted in minutes, not hours.

nodes.label: Basic monitoring
nodes.one_line: Add logging and error tracking so a production failure surfaces as an alert instead of a user complaint.

nodes.label: Secrets rotation
nodes.one_line: Manage and rotate production secrets and credentials without an AI session ever seeing or logging them directly.

nodes.label: Codebase map
nodes.one_line: Build and maintain a map of a codebase's modules and boundaries well enough to know where a new AI task belongs.

nodes.label: Convention enforcement
nodes.one_line: Establish and enforce naming and structure conventions so AI-generated code lands where a human would expect it, not wherever the prompt implied.

nodes.label: Dependency boundaries
nodes.one_line: Define which modules may import which others, and catch an AI-generated change that crosses a boundary it shouldn't.

nodes.label: Tech-debt triage
nodes.one_line: Distinguish AI-introduced shortcuts worth fixing now from ones safe to defer, and track the difference somewhere real.

nodes.label: Refactor with an agent
nodes.one_line: Direct an agent through a cross-cutting refactor — rename, restructure — with checkpoints that catch a partial or inconsistent rewrite.

nodes.label: Scaling decision
nodes.one_line: Decide when a growing AI-assisted app needs a real architecture change — splitting a service, adding a queue — versus another prompt-and-patch cycle.

nodes.label: Full-stack integration review
nodes.one_line: Review a full-stack app end to end — frontend, backend, data, deploy — as one coherent system before calling it production-ready.
